title: A yearly third harmonic absorbs 97 to 98 percent of a 121.54-day wave in 217 GJ 191 HARPS nights
abstract: We test whether the reported 121.54-day signal of Kapteyn's star can be separated from a 121.75-day annual harmonic at the measured HARPS times. With group offsets, group trends, a 48.616-day nuisance wave, and 1.5 m/s added night noise, the annual wave absorbs 97.17 to 98.24 percent of the signal energy in 217 nights. An exact Gaussian distance bound limits power to 0.459 to 0.605 at size 0.05 for a 2.25 m/s circular wave, even for an ideal test that knows the phase. Formal errors alone raise the power bound to 0.926 to 0.981. The annual model gives slightly smaller fit error in four reductions, but these share spectra. The result shows a cadence and noise ambiguity. It does not identify an annual instrument error, exclude planets, or confirm a new signal. Independent velocities were not obtained. Code, source hashes, aggregate results, a figure, a proof, and reproduction steps are included. External raw data and record-level tables remain outside this baseline publication.
